source_text: Proba ergo hoc in eis, quod gratiae Christi apostolus Paulus ascripsit, impleri, videlicet ut ex multis delictis iustificationem operetur, id est ut iustitiam peccatorum plurium una semel remissione contribuat; aut ergo doce parvulos multis obnoxios esse criminibus, ut eis quoque illud persuadeas convenire, in quo laudem munificentiae Christi Apostolus collocavit, ut ex multis eos constet liberatos esse peccatis; aut confitere Paulum nihil in his locis de parvulis, nihil de hominum disputasse natura, quando ea dimitti gratiae liberalitate testatus est, quae te quoque annuente nequeunt in nascentibus inveniri.
pass_a_gloss: Prove therefore that this is fulfilled in them, which the apostle Paul ascribed to the grace of Christ, namely that it works justification from many offenses, that is that it contributes the justice of several sinners by one remission once; either therefore teach that little children are liable to many crimes, so that you may also persuade that that fits them in which the Apostle placed the praise of the munificence of Christ, so that they stand as having been freed from many sins; or confess that Paul disputed nothing in these places about little children, nothing about the nature of human beings, when he testified that those things are dismissed by the liberality of grace which, with you also nodding, cannot be found in those being born.

lemmas.lexica: LS delictum; Blaise Rom 5 delictum vs donum
LS iustificatio; Blaise forensic making-just, not later system
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS gratia=favor; Blaise grace; in iustitia definitions often 'favoritism'

pass_b_english: Prove, then, that what the apostle Paul attributed to Christ’s grace is fulfilled in them: namely, that it produces justification from many offenses, bestowing righteousness through a single, once-for-all remission of many sins. Either show that infants are liable for many crimes, so as to persuade us that the feature in which the apostle placed his praise of Christ’s generosity applies to them too, and that they have been freed from many sins; or confess that Paul discussed neither infants nor human nature in these passages, since he testified that grace’s generosity forgives things which, even with your agreement, cannot be found in newborn children (compare Romans 5:16) (Romans 5:16).

choices.why: Paul's delictum of the one man; an act, not a nature.
Paul's iustificatio vitae; keep forensic making-just, not a later systematic slogan as default.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
